figures.caption: Fig. 1. (A) Training of the contextual contrastive decoder. A shared MEG encoder is trained with two InfoNCE objectives: frame-level alignment to wav2vec 2.0 and word-level alignment to GPT-2 hidden states, combined with weight λe. (B) Neuralconstrained beam search at inference. At each position t, the frozen MEG decoder selects the top-k candidate words Vt, and the frozen LLM scores each candidate given each beam’s decoded history. The normalized MEG and LLM scores are fused with weight α and added to the beam’s cumulative score, and the B highest-scoring sequences are retained.

Fig. 3. Comparison of the neural–language balance for listened and mapped imagined MEG. Top left and middle: word accuracy across α for different candidate-set sizes k at B = 3, with lighter-colored curves for smaller k; shaded regions denote SEM across subjects, markers indicate α∗ for each k, and the y-axes differ across panels. Top right: relative gain over MEG-only (α = 0) at the selected α∗, with one square per held-out subject, lines linking the same subject across conditions, and bars showing mean ± SEM. Bottom: α∗ for each k, with one circle per k and dashed lines marking the mean per condition. Mapped imagined responses show a higher optimal α and a larger gain than listened responses.
